title: Orphan apply/factor artifact-cleanup branches in _finalize_solve_result are unreachable
description: After a successful terminal transition, both post-transition cleanup branches are guarded by `updated_job.get("artifact_handles") is not artifact_handles`. This identity comparison can never be True on the only path where it is evaluated (updated_job is not None), so neither cleanup branch can ever run. The branches are dead code.
evidence: JobLifecycle.transition (src/haute/routes/_job_lifecycle.py:136-168) returns a non-None job ONLY via _store_merged_job_locked, which builds `merged = {**old, **fields}` (src/haute/routes/_job_store.py:252) where `fields` is our `completion_fields` containing the `artifact_handles` key (line 2266). `**fields` copies the reference, so `merged["artifact_handles"] is artifact_handles` is True. _prepare_heavy_object_policy_locked only touches _HEAVY_OBJECT_KEYS=(solver, solve_result, quote_grid, factors_df, ratebook_factor_contexts) (_job_store.py:31) and never `artifact_handles`. The only None returns from transition are the explicit `return None` paths (lines 150,153,155), and because every call here passes `to="completed"`, line 152 (`if ... or to == "completed": return None`) forces None whenever old_status != "running". Therefore: updated_job is None => the earlier block (lines 2285-2299) handles cleanup and returns; updated_job is not None => updated_job.get('artifact_handles') IS artifact_handles, so `is not artifact_handles` at lines 2302 and 2311 is always False. The bodies at 2304-2308 and 2313-2317 are unreachable.
behavior_preservation: Removing both branches preserves behaviour exactly: they never execute. The genuine orphan-cleanup case (transition skipped) is fully handled by the `if updated_job is None:` block at lines 2285-2299.
